title: Compact Error Cards + Command Palette grooming
content:
Goal: Draft UX and backlog for two lightweight but high-leverage features: 1) Compact Error Cards (inline) in the request timeline and 2) a Command Palette for quick triage actions. These are intended to reduce MTTR for engineers and provide a fast path for common remediation actions without leaving the console.

Why now
- Increasing customer asks around ‘fast triage’ instead of full incident investigation. Teams want to skim and act on noisy error surfaces quickly.
- Existing investigator/tracing flows are powerful but heavyweight. We need an intermediary that sits between the timeline list and full investigator workbench.
- Low engineering risk: mostly UI/UX plus wiring to existing trace/replay APIs and rollout flags.

Design principles
- Scannable: show the minimal set of facts per error that answer "what happened" and "what can I do now".
- Actionable: every card should expose 1–3 context-aware next actions (replay, annotate, open trace, pin, create ticket).
- Lightweight: cards should be visually compact and usable in dense timelines and on mobile widths.
- Progressive enhancement: cards initially show summary; expand to reveal trace snippets and suggested root-cause hints.

Compact Error Card – fields (one-line card)
- visual badge: error type (timeout / 5xx / model-error / rate-limit) with color and icon
- timestamp (relative) + request_id (click to copy)
- route / endpoint
- model variant (if applicable)
- latency or time-to-error (ms)
- token_count (if available) as small pill
- top error message (truncated)
- primary action button (contextual): Replay | Retry | Escalate
- kebab menu for secondary actions: open full trace, add note, tag customer-impact, open in investigator

Expanded card (hover or click)
- 1–2 transcribed trace snippets (span names) with earliest error span highlighted
- histogram sparkline for latency distribution for that route in last 5m
- quick suggestions: e.g., "high-latency cluster -> try smaller batch / pin to low-latency pool" or "model exception: fallback to variant v2-quant"
- confidence score for suggested action (low/med/high) derived from heuristics (placeholder)

Interaction notes
- keyboard focusable; Enter expands, Space opens primary action
- swipe-to-dismiss on mobile (archives card to history)
- hover shows tooltip with exact timestamp and full error text
- cards are aware of rollout state: if request was served by canary, show a faint canary pill and link to rollout dashboard

Command Palette – quick triage launcher
- Invoked with Cmd+K / Ctrl+K from within Console
- Search-driven; fuzzy match over actions, ticket templates, and saved triage scripts
- Actions to support initially:
  - Replay request <request_id>
  - Re-run with smaller batch
  - Pin to low-latency pool
  - Open trace in Investigator
  - Create incident (prefilled template)
  - Suggest fallback model variant
  - Annotate request (add note)
- Palette UI shows 1-line description and keyboard hint for each action. When an action requires context (request id), palette pre-fills from selected card or timeline row; if none is selected, palette prompts for the id.

Error grouping and similarity clustering (UX)
- Inline cards support quick "group like errors" action: aggregates by identical top-level error message or by embedding-based similarity (use existing embeddings service).
- Group header shows count, earliest and most recent occurrence, and top 3 routes impacted.
- Action at group level: mute, bulk-annotate, bulk-replay sample (rate-limited), create group incident.

Wireframe sketches (text)
- Timeline view (left column): compact rows for each request
- Right rail: when a row is selected, open a compact card stack with 3 recent related errors and a button "Open investigator".
- Floating Command Palette sits center with translucent backdrop when invoked; suggestions update as user types.
- Minimalist color: use existing console palette; error badge red (#D64937), timeout orange (#F39C12), model-error purple (#7D3C98).

Acceptance criteria (MVP)
- Compact Error Card appears inline in timeline for any request with status != 200
- Primary action button triggers correct backend flows: replay (calls /api/replay), open-trace (links to existing Investigator with request_id), annotate (creates note attached to request)
- Command Palette opens with Cmd/Ctrl+K and can execute at least 4 actions end-to-end (replay, open trace, create incident, annotate)
- Grouping action works for exact string matches and creates group artifact (UI only for MVP; backend grouping later)
- Keyboard and basic accessibility (ARIA labels) implemented

Backlog groom (priority + rough effort)
- MVP: inline cards + basic palette actions (priority: P0, effort: 3 sprints)
- Phase 2: expansion with heuristics/suggestions and grouping header (P1, effort: 2 sprints)
- Phase 3: embeddings-based clustering and bulk-replay workflows + audit logs (P2, effort: 3 sprints)

Dependencies
- Replay API stable (ENG infra already owning; ticket JIRA-ENG-4821)
- Investigator deep-linking contract (platform-engineering)
- Embeddings service for similarity (applied-ml)
- Console keyboard shortcut framework (dev-exp)

Open questions / trade-offs
- Do we rate-limit inline replay from the UI? (Propose: yes, backend enforces 5/min per team; show rate-limit toast)
- Should suggested actions surface ML model suggestions server-side or client heuristics? (Prefer server-side scoring to keep client lightweight)
- Where do we persist group artifacts? (Initial approach: UI-only grouping with ability to export to ticket)

Testing scenarios
- Timeout: simulate request that hangs then times out; card shows timeout badge, suggested action: replay with increased timeout or route to fallback model
- 5xx spike: multiple identical 5xx across routes -> group header shows top routes and allow bulk annotate
- Model error (invalid tokenization): card highlights model variant and suggests fallback; command palette pre-fills model argument

Next steps (this doc)
- Present to console PM and infra in next grooming (agenda: confirm acceptance criteria and replay API contract)
- Create engineering spikes for Command Palette index and for card perf impact
- Design to produce final mockups for handoff to frontend

Notes to reviewer
- This intentionally keeps cards very compact; we reserved full investigator flows for deeper analysis. Looking for feedback on card density, primary action choices, and whether grouping should live inline or be surfaced in a separate "error clusters" view.

Sketch references / handoff
- attach when available: high-fidelity mockups (Figma link placeholder), keyboard interaction spec
